stem: A patient at risk of opioid overdose asks a Massachusetts pharmacy for a prescription-labeled naloxone product. The patient has no patient-specific naloxone prescription, but the pharmacy participates in an authorized statewide standing-order prescription pathway. What is the key legal point?

choices.text: A patient-specific office prescription is the only lawful pharmacy pathway for naloxone.
The standing-order pathway may authorize dispensing when its requirements are met, so absence of a separate patient-specific prescription is not automatically disqualifying.
A standing order can be used only for Schedule II opioids and never for an opioid antagonist.
The pharmacist must convert naloxone into a controlled-substance Schedule before the standing order can be used.
Standing-order authority applies only when the requester is a family member rather than the person at risk.

explanation.core_reasoning: Massachusetts pharmacy naloxone access can operate through an authorized standing order. The pharmacist should determine whether that pathway applies rather than assuming that only a conventional patient-specific prescription can support dispensing.

choice_analysis.A: Massachusetts provides a broader pharmacy access mechanism than a patient-specific prescription alone.
choice_analysis.B: A valid standing order can supply the prescribing authority for an otherwise eligible naloxone dispensing encounter.
choice_analysis.C: The standing-order mechanism is not limited to dispensing the opioids that naloxone is intended to reverse.
choice_analysis.D: Naloxone’s access does not require assigning it a federal controlled-substance schedule.
choice_analysis.E: The pathway can serve the person at risk as well as other qualifying recipients.

related_facts: The statewide standing order can serve as prescription authority for prescription naloxone when its requirements are met.
FDA-labeled OTC naloxone is a separate product and does not become Schedule VI merely because prescription naloxone also exists.
explanation.mpje_trap: Ask what authority supports the dispensing, not whether a traditional prescription sheet exists.

reasoning_steps: Identify the absence of a patient-specific prescription
Determine whether the standing order can support the naloxone dispensing
